text: Bachelor of Science in Information Systems The Bachelor of Science in Information Systems (BSIS) at Talibon Polytechnic College is a 4-year program focusing on designing and implementing computer-based information systems and ICT solutions to meet business needs. It equips students with skills in systems development, business process analysis, and ICT implementation. Graduates can work as Systems Analysts, IT Project Managers, or Information Security Specialists.

Narisma Achievements 2025 BSIS Department || Community Outreach " Basic Computer Literacy Skills Program" with Zamora, Talibon, Bohol For the past two days, the BSIS Department conducted the Basic Computer Literacy Skills Program, a community outreach initiative in partnership with the Barangay Officials of Zamora, Talibon, Bohol.

The two-day activity featured a series of educational sessions designed to help the officials deepen their understanding of computer literacy, documentation, and digital communication—essential skills that can make their daily responsibilities more efficient and effective.

With the support of the TPC Administration, the BSIS Faculty, and a few selected BSIS student officers, the team successfully facilitated the training and workshop, ensuring that the participants gained confidence and familiarity in using computers.

We extend our heartfelt appreciation to the TPC Administration, the BSIS Faculty, the dedicated student officers, and the Barangay Officials of Barangay Zamora for their cooperation, enthusiasm, and commitment that made this program meaningful and impactful. BSIS Course Description Catalog (excerpt) CC 100 - Introduction to Computing Foundational course covering computer hardware/software basics, number systems, and problem-solving concepts before formal programming begins. CC 101 - Computer Programming 1 Introduces programming fundamentals: variables, control structures, functions, and basic data types through small console programs.

CC 102 - Computer Programming 2 Builds on CC 101 with object-oriented programming: classes, objects, inheritance, and polymorphism. CC 103 - Data Structures and Algorithms Covers arrays, linked lists, stacks, queues, trees, and sorting/searching algorithms, with emphasis on choosing the right structure for a problem. CC 104 - Information Management Covers relational database design, normalization, SQL, and data modeling for information systems.

CC 105 - Application Development and Emerging Technologies Hands-on application-building course integrating current tools/platforms (e.g. APIs, cloud, or mobile) into a working multi-module system. IPT 101 - Integrative Programming and Technologies Covers integrating multiple programming languages/technologies (e.g. a web front end, backend services, and APIs) into one cohesive application.

HCI 1 - Human Computer Interaction Covers usability principles, interface design, and evaluating software from the end user's perspective. IS 104 - System Analysis & Design Teaches requirements gathering, process modeling (DFDs, use cases), and translating business needs into system specifications. IS 107 - Software Engineering Covers the software development lifecycle, methodologies (e.g. Agile/Scrum), and software quality/testing practices.

BSIS Program - Enrollment, Prerequisites, and Academic Standing Policy Prerequisite enforcement: a student may not enroll in a course until every prerequisite listed for it in the curriculum checklist has been passed (grade of 3.00 or better). Registration will be blocked for any course whose prerequisite is missing, failed, or currently "in progress" in the same term.

Course load: a regular BSIS student may enroll in a maximum of 24 units per regular semester (Year 1-4 Sem 1/Sem 2) and 9 units in the summer term. A student on academic probation is capped at 15 units per regular semester until good standing is restored. Academic standing: - Good Standing: term GWA of 3.00 or better with no more than one failing grade in the current term.

- Probation: a student who fails 2 or more courses in a single term, or whose cumulative GWA falls below 3.00, is placed on academic probation for the following term. - Dismissal: a student placed on probation for two consecutive terms, or who fails the same required course three times, is subject to academic dismissal from the BSIS program, pending an appeal to the Program Head.

Capstone eligibility: enrollment in CAP 101 (Capstone Project I) requires 3rd Year Standing, per the curriculum checklist. Enrollment in CAP 102 (Capstone Project II) requires completion of CAP 101. Enrollment in PRACTICUM (Practicum for Information Systems, 486 hours) requires 4th Year Standing. Add/drop: students may add or drop a course only within the first two (2) weeks of a regular semester (first week for the summer term), subject to the Registrar's published academic calendar.

BSIS Program - Grading System and GWA Policy Numeric grades range from 1.00 (highest) to 5.00 (failing), following the standard Philippine collegiate scale used across TPC programs: 1.00 = 97-100% 2.00 = 83-86% 3.00 = 75-77% 1.25 = 94-96% 2.25 = 80-82% 5.00 = Below 75% (Failed) 1.50 = 91-93% 2.50 = 77-79% INC = Incomplete 1.75 = 88-90% 2.75 = 75-77% DRP = Dropped A student's General Weighted Average (GWA) is the unit-weighted mean of all numeric grades for the term: sum(grade x units) / sum(units).

Latin honors eligibility (Cum Laude and above) requires a cumulative GWA of 1.75 or better with no grade lower than 2.5 in any course, and no record of a failing (5.00) grade in any course throughout the program. A student who receives INC must complete the missing requirement within one (1) year, or the grade automatically converts to 5.00 (Failed).
